verdict.rationale: Published GOV.UK guidance pages (VAT registration, Corporation Tax, MTD sign-up, register as employer) were retrieved as readable text, which implies the main public reading surface is reachable without a bot wall, JS-only shell or CAPTCHA. However, the developer hub's robots.txt disallows every crawler except Googlebot. That puts HMRC's own API documentation off-limits to a respectful identified agent, so only part of the public reading surface is open. Missing for 10: an explicit probe confirming HTTP 200 for GOV.UK guidance with a standard identified user agent, agent access to the developer-hub documentation, and independent confirmation that no CAPTCHA or JS gate exists.

support.subject: As an AI-native founder, the service's published guidance pages are reachable by a keyless agent with a standard identified user agent — no bot wall, JS-only shell, or CAPTCHA in front of the public reading surface
